business_model.claim: Domestic metallurgical contracts are typically annual fixed-price agreements priced FOB at the mine on a short ton basis (with customers bearing onward transportation), whereas international contracts are typically priced FOB at the outbound shipping port on a metric ton basis (with Alpha bearing mine-to-port transportation).
quotes: Domestic met customers typically enter into one-year agreements with a fixed price for the entire contract year.
Our domestic sales contracts are typically priced free on board (“FOB”) at our mines and on a short ton basis.
Our international sales contracts are typically priced FOB at the shipping port from which such coal is delivered and on a metric ton basis.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in 10-K MD&A [P3] and 10-Q MD&A [P4].
business_model.claim: Global steel demand and metallurgical coal pricing are primary revenue drivers: weak steel demand drove a 28.0% drop in coal revenues in 2025 to $2,122,605 (table in thousands) from $2,946,579 (table in thousands) in 2024 as average realization fell 19.3% and tons sold declined 10.8%.
quotes: The decrease was primarily due to a 19.3% decline in average coal sales realization as metallurgical coal pricing declined significantly as a result of weakened global steel demand.
Coal sales volumes also declined 10.8% due to weaker demand.
Met coal prices continue to be restrained by weak global steel demand.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in 10-K MD&A [P3] and 10-Q MD&A [P4].
business_model.claim: Realized pricing per ton also moves with coal quality (especially lower volatile matter, which produces a higher coke yield and commands higher prices), regional supply-demand balances, and benchmark index spreads.
quotes: Coal volatility is a significant factor influencing met coal pricing as coal with a lower volatility has historically been more highly valued and typically commands a higher price in the market.
The volatility of met coal determines the percentage of feed coal that becomes coke, known as coke yield, with lower volatility producing a higher coke yield.

The increase was primarily attributable to a 5.0% increase in our average coal sales realization as sales shifted toward relatively higher quality coal with stronger pricing in the current year period.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Risk Factors [P2], 10-K MD&A [P3], and 10-Q MD&A [P4].
business_model.claim: Revenue is also sensitive to global coal supply disruptions, tariffs and retaliatory trade barriers, U.S. dollar exchange rate movements, and North American steelmakers shifting toward non-coke electric arc furnaces.
quotes: Supply-related issues, including December 2025 and January 2026 flooding in Queensland, Australia, impacted metallurgical markets in recent months.
The North American steel industry increasingly relies on processes to make steel that do not use coke, such as electric arc furnaces or pulverized coal processes.

Consequently, currency fluctuations could adversely affect the competitiveness of our coal in international markets, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Business [P1], 10-Q MD&A [P4], and Q3 2026 earnings release [P6].
business_model.claim: Shipment volume and timing depend on CSX and Norfolk Southern rail service and port capacity at Dominion Terminal Associates (65.0% owned by Alpha), where June 2026 storm damage to a stacker reclaimer delayed shipments and requires utilizing other Hampton Roads terminals.
quotes: We own a 65.0% interest in Dominion Terminal Associates (“DTA”), a coal export terminal in Newport News, Virginia.

Additionally, refer to “Liquidity and Capital Resources - Business Updates” for developments regarding a key piece of equipment, a stacker reclaimer machine at Dominion Terminal Associates (“DTA”), which sustained significant damage due to high winds from a storm as previously announced in June 2026.

Additionally, we are confident in our plans to minimize the disruption to our sales and logistics processes by also utilizing our throughput capacity at other Hampton Roads terminals while work is underway to replace the damaged machinery at DTA.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K MD&A [P3], 10-Q MD&A [P4], and Q3 2026 earnings release [P6].
business_model.claim: Core cost of coal sales ($1,924,691 (table in thousands) in 2025 and $1,427,708 (table in thousands) in the 2026 nine-month period) is driven by production and sales volumes, purchased coal, wages and benefits, healthcare, contract services, and volatile inputs including fuel, explosives, steel, tires, electricity, and repairs.
quotes: Our primary expenses are for operating supply costs, repair and maintenance expenditures, costs of purchased coal, royalties, wages and benefits, freight and handling costs and taxes incurred in selling our coal.

We experience volatility in operating costs related to fuel, explosives, steel, tires, contract services and healthcare, among others, and take measures to mitigate the increases in these costs at all operations.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in 10-K MD&A [P3].
business_model.claim: Freight and handling costs move with export share and shipping points while royalties and taxes move with coal prices; in 2025, lower export share, lower coal-price-linked royalties and taxes, lower purchased coal, and wage and higher-cost production cuts drove a 12.0% decline in average cost of coal sales per ton.
quotes: Average cost of coal sales per ton decreased 12.0% compared to the prior year period, due in part to a reduction in freight and handling costs as a relatively lower percentage of export sales resulted in lower rail and ocean vessel freight costs.
The lower coal pricing environment reduced royalties and taxes.

In addition, lower levels of purchased coal and the ongoing impact of cost reduction efforts, including wage reductions during the second quarter of 2025, as well as the impact of previous decisions to reduce relatively higher-cost production sources served to reduce costs on a per ton basis.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K [P1, P2, P3] and Q3 2026 earnings release guidance [P6].
business_model.claim: Unit costs and cash outlays are also affected by Central Appalachian geology, mine curtailments and idlings (such as Checkmate Powellton and Long Branch), and ongoing idle operations expense guided at $24 to $32 (table in millions) for 2026 and $25 to $33 (table in millions) for 2027.
quotes: Our Checkmate Powellton mine, which was in its early stages of operations and had relatively higher costs, was idled during the fourth quarter of 2024.
In addition, our Long Branch surface mine was idled in the first quarter of 2025 and production levels were reduced at our Jerry Fork and Black Eagle mines during 2025.
Idle operations expense is expected to be between $25 million and $33 million.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-Q statement of operations [F2] and 10-K MD&A [P3].
business_model.claim: Operating results also reflect non-cash and overhead charges including depreciation, depletion, and amortization (174,524 (table in thousands) in 2025; 111,456 (table in thousands) in the 2026 nine-month period), asset retirement obligation accretion (22,126 (table in thousands) in 2025; 15,678 (table in thousands) in the 2026 nine-month period), and SG&A expenses (60,158 (table in thousands) in 2025; 52,523 (table in thousands) in the 2026 nine-month period).
quotes: Depreciation, depletion and amortization increased $7.2 million, or 4.3%, for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the prior year period.
Selling, general and administrative expenses decreased $13.8 million, or 18.7%, for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the prior year period.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-Q balance sheet [F1] and 10-K Risk Factors [P2].
business_model.claim: Environmental and MSHA safety regulations impose substantial compliance costs alongside long-term workers' compensation and black lung obligations (183,438 (table in thousands)), pension obligations (67,108 (table in thousands)), and asset retirement obligations (200,994 (table in thousands)).
quotes: We incur substantial costs to comply with the laws, regulations and permits that apply to our mining and other operations and to address the outcome of inspections.

These factors have had and will continue to have a significant effect on our costs of production and competitive position and, as a result, on our results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K MD&A non-GAAP reconciliations [P3] and Q3 2026 earnings release tables [P6].
business_model.claim: Alpha's operating cash margin per ton tracks the spread between non-GAAP coal sales realization and non-GAAP cost of coal sales, which compressed from $142.66 versus $112.01 ($30.64 margin per ton) in 2024 to $117.08 versus $102.23 ($14.85 margin per ton) in 2025, and stood at $121.40 versus $106.03 ($15.37 margin per ton) in the 2026 nine-month period.
quotes: Non-GAAP coal margin per ton for our coal operations is calculated as non-GAAP coal sales realization per ton for our coal operations less non-GAAP cost of coal sales per ton for our coal operations.
The decrease was primarily due to a $25.58, or 17.9%, decline in non-GAAP coal sales realization per ton as weakened global steel demand reduced metallurgical coal pricing.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited 10-K Risk Factors
competitive_position.claim: Alpha faces competition from domestic and international coal producers where industry overcapacity, favorable foreign trade policies, or foreign currency depreciation against the U.S. dollar can give overseas rivals a pricing advantage.
quotes: We compete with numerous other coal producers in various regions of the U.S. for domestic and international sales.
Subsequent overcapacity in the industry contributed, and may in the future contribute, to lower coal prices.

Coal is priced internationally in U.S. dollars, and, as a result, general economic conditions in foreign markets and changes in foreign currency exchange rates may provide our foreign competitors with a competitive advantage.

competitive_position.claim: Weak global steel demand, additional U.S. High-Vol. coal supply, and U.S. and retaliatory foreign tariffs threaten Alpha's realized prices and export demand, after non-GAAP coal sales realization per ton declined 17.9% in 2025.
quotes: However, Alpha’s export customers include foreign steel producers who may be markedly affected by these and similar tariffs to the extent their imports into the U.S. are curtailed as a result of tariffs.
The decrease was primarily due to a $25.58, or 17.9%, decline in non-GAAP coal sales realization per ton as weakened global steel demand reduced metallurgical coal pricing.
Met coal prices continue to be restrained by weak global steel demand.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited 10-K Risk Factors
competitive_position.claim: Rising North American reliance on non-coke steelmaking processes such as electric arc furnaces and pulverized coal injection, alongside steel substitutes, threatens long-term metallurgical coal volume and pricing.
quotes: The North American steel industry increasingly relies on processes to make steel that do not use coke, such as electric arc furnaces or pulverized coal processes.

As this trend continues, the amount of met coal that we sell and the prices that we receive for it in North America could decrease, thereby reducing our revenues and adversely impacting our earnings and the value of our coal reserves.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited 10-K Risk Factors
competitive_position.claim: Customer concentration poses a revenue and credit threat because Alpha's largest customer accounted for approximately 14% and its 10 largest customers accounted for approximately 77% of total revenues in 2025.
quotes: Coal sales to our largest customer during the year ended December 31, 2025 accounted for approximately 14% of our total revenues, and coal sales to our 10 largest customers accounted for approximately 77% of our total revenues.
In addition, purchasers of our met coal may increasingly be required to implement costly new emissions and other technologies, thereby increasing the risk we bear for customer payment default.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited 10-K Risk Factors
competitive_position.claim: Fossil-fuel lending and insurance restrictions, ESG divestment pressures, and stricter environmental and mine-safety regulations threaten Alpha's financing, surety bonding, permits, and cost structure.
quotes: Certain financial institutions, including banks and insurance companies, have adopted policies that prevent or limit those institutions from providing financing, insurance, bonding, and other services to entities that produce, generate power from or use fossil fuels.

Concerns associated with global climate change, and GHG emissions reduction initiatives designed to address them, have resulted, and are expected to continue to result, in materially increased operating costs for steel producers who use met coal, particularly in Europe.
MSHA and state regulators may also order the temporary or permanent closing of a mine in the event of certain violations of safety rules, accidents or imminent dangers.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited 10-Q and 8-K earnings release
competitive_position.claim: Export throughput and production stability face physical and operating hazards, including the June 2026 storm damage to a stacker reclaimer at DTA, difficult geology, labor shortages, and critical input shortages.
quotes: Additionally, refer to “Liquidity and Capital Resources - Business Updates” for developments regarding a key piece of equipment, a stacker reclaimer machine at Dominion Terminal Associates (“DTA”), which sustained significant damage due to high winds from a storm as previously announced in June 2026.
Despite what is expected to be a lengthy timeline for replacing the damaged equipment, we do not anticipate significant capital outlays in association with the replacement process.

We may also experience difficult geologic conditions, delays in obtaining permits, labor shortages, unforeseen equipment problems, and unexpected shortages of critical materials such as tires, fuel and explosives that may result in adverse cost increases and limit our ability to produce at forecasted levels.
